findings.title: Substring match on 'event.type:error' accepts negated and mixed queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the lowercased query string contains `event.type:error`. That also matches `!event.type:error`, `event.type:transaction OR event.type:error`, and `event.type:error_foo`. For the discover dataset, any of these queries gets `count()` rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)`. Negated or mixed queries include transactions, which have no sample_weight, so the endpoint returns wrong counts. The check should parse the query (or inspect the search filters) and require a positive, exclusive `event.type:error` filter.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses outer dataset and raw request query, not the actual scoped query
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` passes the closed-over `dataset` and `request` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. It ignores the `scoped_dataset` and `query` arguments it was called with. In the dashboard split flow, the outer dataset is metrics_enhanced while the call runs against `discover` with an `!event.type:transaction` errors-only query. Upsampling is therefore never applied to error results there. In general the decision can disagree with the query actually executed. The function should use `scoped_dataset` and the effective `query` string.

findings.title: Aliasing to 'count' changes the result key away from the requested 'count()' column
findings.body: `count()` is rewritten to `upsampled_count() as count`, so the result column is named `count`, while the rest of the stats pipeline and the client key results by the requested yAxis `count()`. With multiple yAxis values, the per-axis lookup/serialization can fail to find `count()` data. Top-events ordering on `-count()` also no longer refers to a selected column. The upsampled output should keep the original column name, e.g. alias `count()`, or the mapping should be handled explicitly.

findings.title: upsampled_count sums sample_weight with no null/default handling
findings.body: `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` assumes every event has `sample_weight`. Errors ingested before the project was allowlisted, or without client sampling context, will have null or zero weight. Those events contribute 0, so counts come out lower than plain `count()` and are not upsampled correctly. The comment asserts a schema guarantee that the PR does nothing to enforce. Use something like `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))`.

findings.title: Eligibility cache is never invalidated; invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code
findings.body: Eligibility is cached for 60s under a key derived from the org and the project id set. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere, and an option change cannot enumerate every cached project combination anyway. After the allowlist changes, queries keep returning stale upsampled or non-upsampled counts for up to 60s. The only cost avoided is an in-memory options lookup, so the cache adds an extra network round trip and stale-state risk for little benefit. The 'cached result ensures consistent behavior' comment in the endpoint is also wrong: the check is re-run on every `_get_event_stats` call.

findings.title: Accidental submodule gitlink committed
findings.body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink pointing at the base commit, with no matching .gitmodules entry. This looks like a stray nested checkout. It will break clones and CI submodule handling and should be removed.

findings.title: Cache key relies on Python hash() of the project tuple
findings.body: The cache key embeds `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Hash collisions between different project sets would share a cached eligibility value, which could wrongly upsample a set containing non-allowlisted projects. Use a stable, collision-free representation, such as the joined ids or a sha of them.
